chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His Exalted and Mighty saying: 'And do not make your hand [be] chained to your neck,' he said: He gathered his hand, then said: 'Like this.' And: 'Nor extend it completely,' he said: He spread his palm and said: 'Like this.'

key_terms.الْبَسْطِ: Extension or spreading out, indicating generosity or excess
key_terms.رَاحَتَهُ: His palm, the part of the hand spread to show openness
key_terms.عُنُقِكَ: Your neck, metaphorically indicating the hand is tied to the body
key_terms.مَغْلُولَةً: Chained or bound, indicating holding back or miserliness

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq explain the meaning of 'chained hand' and 'fully extended hand' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a tangible exegesis of Surah Al-Isra 17:29 by physically demonstrating the extremes of miserliness (chaining the hand) and extravagance (fully extending the palm). This practical commentary underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *wasatiyyah* (moderation) in financial conduct, balancing the duty of charity with the preservation of one's own livelihood.
